questions.question: Which among the following international boundaries is the longest?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The international border between India and Bangladesh is currently considered the longest land border between two countries. It spans approximately 4,096 kilometers (2,545 miles) in length.**
 
• The border between** India and Bangladesh** is a complex and diverse boundary that runs across various states and regions, and it is an important aspect of the bilateral relations between the two countries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The international border between India and Myanmar (formerly known as Burma) is approximately 1,643 kilometers (1,020 miles) in length.**

 
 
• It stretches from the tri-junction of India,** Myanmar, and Bangladesh in the east to the tri-junction of India, Myanmar, and China in the north.**
 
• The border runs through the northeastern states of India, including **Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur, and Mizoram.**
 
• It is an important border for trade, cultural exchanges, and regional cooperation between India and Myanmar.
 
 
 
• **The international border between India and China, often referred to as the Line of Actual Control (LAC), stretches approximately 3,488 kilometers (2,167 miles) in length.**
 
 
• It spans from the easternmost point of the Indian state of Jammu and Kashmir in the west to the tri-junction of India, China, and Myanmar in the east.
 
• The border passes through various regions, including Ladakh, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Sikkim, and Arunachal Pradesh.
 
• The Indo-China border is a disputed boundary, and both countries have experienced tensions and conflicts along certain sectors of the border over the years.
 
 
 
• **The international border between India and Pakistan, known as the Line of Control (LoC), spans approximately 2,300 kilometers (1,430 miles)**.
 
 
• It runs from the northernmost point of India in the state of Jammu and Kashmir, extends westward across the states of Punjab and Rajasthan, and ends at the Arabian Sea in the state of Gujarat.
 
• The Indo-Pak border is a heavily guarded and sensitive boundary due to the historical and ongoing conflicts between the two countries.
 
• It is monitored and patrolled by security forces from both India and Pakistan.

questions.question: Under which article of the Indian constitution is the Prime Minister the head of the Council of Ministers?

• The Prime Minister provides advice to the President, who acts in accordance with that advice while performing their functions.

• **Article 52** establishes the President as the **Head of State in India.**
 
• It outlines that the President holds powers, duties, and functions as per the Constitution and is vested with executive powers, including those specifically mentioned in the Constitution.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of Phylum – Annelida?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 3**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An example of the **phylum Annelida** is the **earthworm**.
 
• **Earthworms** belong to the class** Clitellata** within the **phylum Annelida.**
 
• They are segmented worms characterized by their long, **cylindrical bodies** divided into **numerous repeated segments**.
 
• **Earthworms **are commonly found in soil and play a vital role in the ecosystem by enhancing soil fertility through their burrowing and decomposition activities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Hookworms** are** parasitic worms** that infect the s**mall intestine of humans and other animals.**

 
 
• There are two main species of hookworm that commonly infect humans: **Ancylostoma duodenale and Necator americanus.**
 
• These worms are named for their hook-like mouthparts, which they use to attach to the intestinal lining and feed on blood.
 
• **Hookworm infection** occurs when a person comes into contact with contaminated soil or feces that contain hookworm larvae.
 
• The larvae can penetrate **the skin, usually through bare feet, and migrate through the bloodstream to reach the lungs.**
 
• From there, they are coughed up and swallowed, eventually reaching the small intestine where they mature into adult worms. Adult hookworms then attach to the intestinal wall and start feeding on blood, which can lead to iron deficiency anemia.
 
 
 
• **Filaria worms, also known as filarial nematodes, are a group of parasitic worms that belong to the family Filariidae.**
 
 
• These worms are responsible for causing a group of diseases known as **filariasis or lymphatic filariasis.**
 
• **Filariasis** is a tropical and subtropical disease that affects millions of people worldwide, particularly in regions such as Africa, Southeast Asia, and the Pacific Islands.
 
 
 
• **Roundworms, also known as nematodes, are a diverse group of worms that belong to the phylum Nematoda.**
 
• They are among the most common animals on Earth and can be found in a wide range of** environments, including soil, freshwater, and marine habitats**.
 
• Some roundworms are free-living, while others are parasitic and can infect **plants, animals, and humans.**

questions.question: Cheetahs brought from Namibia were introduced in the Kuno National Park located in ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Madhya Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Prime Minister Narendra Modi will release Cheetahs in Kuno National Park in Madhya Pradesh on September 17, under Project Cheetah.
 
• Project Cheetah is the world’s first inter-continental large wild carnivore translocation project.
 
• Cheetahs that will be introduced are from Namibia and have been brought under an MoU signed earlier this year.
 
• They will help in the restoration of open forest and grassland ecosystems in India.
 
• Eight cheetahs, five females and three males will be brought to Gwalior from Namibia in a special Boeing 747-400 aircraft, covering over 8,000km distance in over 20 hours.
 
• A team from Namibia’s Cheetah Conservation Foundation (CCF) will also be with the animals.
 
• This will help conserve biodiversity and enhance the ecosystem services like water security, carbon sequestration, and soil moisture conservation.
 
• The Cheetah Reintroduction Project is supported by Indian Oil and steered by National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA), and will formally take off on September 17.
 
• Indian Oil will support NTCA with ₹50.22 crores, as part of its CSR, to take this project forward.
 
• Indian Oil’s financial support would be directed towards Cheetah introduction endeavors, Habitat management, protection, eco-development, staff training, and veterinary healthcare.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• In this martial art form when unarmed combat is involved or no weapon is used while performing it, then it is known as Sarit Sarak.
 
• It is also known as HUYEN LALLONG and CHEBI GATKA.​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Muay Thai, also known as Thai boxing, is a combat sport of Thailand that uses stand-up striking along with various clinching techniques.
 
• This discipline is known as the "**Art of eight limbs**", as it is characterised by the combined use of fists, elbows, knees, and shins. 
 
 

 
• Kalaripayattu

 
 
• Kalaripayattu is a martial art.
 
• It originated in Kerala from the 3rd century BC to the 2nd century AD.
 
• The place where this martial art is practised is called a 'Kalari'.
 
• It is considered to be among the oldest martial arts still in existence.
 
 

 
• **Gatka**

 
 
• Gatka__ is a __form of martial arts__ performed by the __Sikhs of Punjab__.

questions.question: Who is the governor of Reserve Bank of India as of 2022?
questions.solution:

Their tenure in office is 5 years for Governor and 4 years for Deputy governor. Also in the organizational structure are Executive Directors.
 
• Presently Shri Shaktikanta Das is the 25th Governor of the Reserve Bank of India since December 2018, who took over the charge from Dr. Urjit Patel. To start with the first person appointed as the Governor of RBI was Sir Osborne Smith.
 
• The RBI Act provides that CBD conducts one meeting every quarter and at least 6 meetings in a year.
 
• Important details about the Governors of RBI:

• Raghuram Rajan: He was the former governor of RBI from 4 September 2013 to 4 September 2016.
 
• Y.V Reddy: He was the former governor of RBI from 6 September 2003 to 5 September 2008.
 
• Urjit Patel: He was the former governor of RBI from 4 September 2016 to 11 December 2018.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a technique or a step to convert normal water to potable water?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bromination**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Bromination: It is not used as a technique to convert normal water to potable water.
 
• While bromine can be used as a disinfectant, it is generally employed in specific industrial or specialized applications, such as swimming pools, spas, or certain water treatment processes.
 
• Bromine's usage for general potable water treatment is not as prevalent as chlorine.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Filtration: Filtration is a common technique used to remove solid particles, sediments, and larger contaminants from water. It involves passing the water through a filtration medium or membrane that traps impurities and allows clean water to pass through.
 
• Boiling: Boiling water is an effective method to kill most types of pathogens, including bacteria, viruses, and parasites. When water is brought to a rolling boil for a certain duration (usually around one minute), it helps in rendering the water safe for consumption by destroying harmful microorganisms.
 
• Chlorination: Chlorination is a widely used method for disinfecting and purifying water. It involves adding a small amount of chlorine, usually in the form of chlorine gas or chlorine compounds like sodium hypochlorite or calcium hypochlorite, to the water. Chlorine acts as a disinfectant, killing bacteria, viruses, and other harmful microorganisms, thus making the water safe to drink.

• Madhubani painting is the folk painting of Bihar.
 
• Jitwarpur village of Madhubani district is the main centre.
 
• In this painting, the** Kohbar (traditional room of the married couple) in the folklore of the Bihar region is drawn as a painting.**
 
• In this style of folk painting, the scenes of Ramayana and the images of Hindu God-Goddesses are depicted on the canvas.
 
• Mahasundari Devi is a famous artist of Madhubani painting.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Madhubani painting, also referred to as Mithila Art (as it flourishes in the Mithila region of Bihar),** is characterized by line drawings filled in with bright colours and contrasts or patterns.
 
• This style of painting has been traditionally done by the women of the region, though today men are also involved to meet the demand.
 
• These paintings are popular because of their tribal motifs and use of bright earthy colours.
 
• These paintings are done with mineral pigments prepared by the artists.
 
• The work is done on freshly plastered or a mud walls.

questions.question: On which of the following dates does the summer solstice falls?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __21 June.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The longest day in the year is 21 June which is generally termed Summer Solstice.
 
• The summer solstice which is generally termed as an estival solstice or midsummer occurs when one of the Earth's poles has its maximum tilt toward the Sun.
 
• It happens twice annually, once in each hemisphere (Northern and Southern).
 
• For that hemisphere, the summer solstice is when the Sun reaches its apex position in the sky and is the day with the longest period of daylight.
 
• Within the Arctic Circle (for the northern hemisphere) or Antarctic Circle (for the southern hemisphere), there is incessant daylight around the summer solstice.
 
• On the summer solstice, the earth's maximum axial tilt toward the Sun is 23.44°.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In addition to, the Sun's declination from the celestial equator is 23.44°.
 
• The summer solstice occurs during the summer period.
 
• This is the June solstice in the Northern Hemisphere and the December solstice in the Southern Hemisphere.
 
• Depending on the shift of the calendar, the summer solstice happens sometime between June 20 and June 22 in the Northern Hemisphere and between December 20 and December 23 in the Southern Hemisphere.
 
• The same dates on the contrary hemisphere are referred to as the winter solstice.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f960670c39b29a24e05ecdaba3bfd9b16f9834751836c02a4d65f07a5de7226b.png]
